sources.citation: Hilty, Holly J. & Jessica R. Mitchell. 2012. Yamphu: A sociolinguistic survey. Kathmandu: Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University & SIL International.

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Bir. 2012. Yamphu and English Pronominals. M.Ed. thesis, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu.
sources.note: p. 9 says Yamphu dialects differ 'in phonology, vocabulary and supra-segmental features level viz. tone, juncture, stress etc.'; Appendix D 'Yamphu Sound Systems' gives vowel/consonant charts only. No rule for stress placement.

sources.citation: Doornenbal, Marius. 2009. A grammar of Bantawa. Utrecht: LOT.

tone.quote: In the 1970s and 1980s, tone was reported in Sunwar (Bieri and Schulze 1971a, 1971b, Genetti 1988), Thulung (Allen, 1975), and Khaling (Toba and Toba 1975), with indications of tonal morphophonology. [...] These three tonal languages occupy a contiguous area in Ramechhap, Okhaldhunga, and Solu Districts in the north-west of the Kiranti range. A tonal opposition reflecting an underlying stem postfinal (§4.2) has been reported in verb forms of a Bantawa dialect, for some speakers only (Doornenbal 2009, cf. Winter 1997).
tone.locator: sec. 2.5 'Tone, Stress', author version p. 7; published chapter pp. 646-679, exact page not established
